sites.name: Memphis / Colossus
sites.dek: SpaceXAI training campus in Memphis and Southaven: Colossus 1 and Colossus II on about 1 gigawatt of company-stated compute power.

location.text: Memphis, Tennessee; Colossus II also in Southaven, Mississippi

status.note: Colossus II still being built out.

powerSegments.text: Both sites together: approximately 1.0 gigawatt of compute power, with additional capacity available (SpaceX prospectus, 12 Jun 2026).

power.text: Colossus 1: more than 300 MW (Anthropic, 6 May 2026). Both sites together: approximately 1.0 gigawatt of compute power, with additional capacity available (SpaceX prospectus, 12 Jun 2026).
power.homesQualifier: at both sites, company-stated compute power

chips.countText: about 110,000 (second Colossus II cluster); at least 220,000 more GB300 in next phase

compute.text: over 1 million H100-equivalents across Colossus I and II at the end of 2025

usedFor.what: training and inference for frontier models, including Grok-5 on Colossus II
all Colossus 1 capacity for Claude Pro and Max users

cooling.text: Liquid cooling; advanced water cleaning, reclamation, and recycling

water.text: Closed-loop reuse; planned $80 million water recycling plant to protect about 4.745 billion gallons of the Memphis Aquifer a year (company claim)

site.text: Colossus 1 on Paul R. Lowry Road, Memphis (repurposed factory shell); Colossus II on Tulane Road, Memphis and Stateline Road, Southaven

onSiteGeneration.text: A 1.2 GW permanent natural gas plant with 41 turbines is under construction in Southaven (Clean Air Act permit, March 2026).

gridNotes.text: 150 MW substation ($35M) plus a second substation ($20M) on the Memphis grid.

image.alt: Aerial view of Colossus in Memphis

notes.text: SpaceXSI plans to equip this facility with 1 million GPUs by 2026.
NAACP v. X.AI Corp. over gas turbines at Colossus II continues: on 19 Oct 2026 the court let the US join the case and refused to dismiss it.

updates.text: First Colossus cluster online in 122 days; first Colossus II cluster in 91 days; both sites together about 1 gigawatt of compute power.
Anthropic uses all Colossus 1 capacity: more than 300 MW and over 220,000 NVIDIA GPUs within the month.
Colossus 1: over 220,000 Nvidia chips, a mix of H100, H200, and GB200.
Colossus I and II ended 2025 above one million H100-equivalents.
Grok 4 training used Colossus, described as a 200,000 GPU cluster.
x.ai/colossus: built in 122 days, doubled to 200,000 GPUs in 92 days; elsewhere on the page, 180,000 H100 GPUs in one cluster.
100,000 Nvidia Hopper GPUs operating in 122 days; plan to double to 200,000 Hopper GPUs.

sites.name: Stargate Abilene
sites.dek: OpenAI's flagship Stargate campus in Abilene, Texas: Crusoe builds it, Oracle runs it on OCI, with GB200 racks.

operator.text: Built by Crusoe; compute on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure

status.note: 6 of 8 buildings delivered to the customer (Oracle, 10 Sep 2026). Crusoe expects campus completion by end of 2026.

statusSegments.text: 6 of 8 buildings delivered to the customer (Oracle, 10 Sep 2026).
Crusoe expects campus completion by end of 2026.

powerSegments.text: 618 MW delivered (6 of 8 buildings, 75% of total capacity per Oracle).
Campus planned at 1.2 GW (8 buildings, about 4 million sq ft).

power.text: 618 MW delivered (6 of 8 buildings, 75% of total capacity per Oracle). Campus planned at 1.2 GW (8 buildings, about 4 million sq ft).

chips.countText: hundreds of thousands of GPUs on one fabric at completion

cooling.text: Direct-to-chip liquid cooling in a closed loop with zero-water evaporation

site.text: 8 buildings planned, about 4 million sq ft

image.alt: Aerial view of Stargate Abilene campus

notes.text: Oracle delivered 131,000 GPUs at Abilene in Q1 FY27 alone (earnings call, 10 Sep 2026). Cumulative site GPU count is not stated in writing.
A separate 900 MW Crusoe campus for Microsoft sits adjacent; it is not the Stargate site.

updates.text: 6 of 8 buildings, 618 MW, and 75% of total capacity delivered; 131,000 GPUs delivered in the quarter.
Phase 2 expected to reach completion by end of 2026.
First phase up on OCI with early training and inference workloads.
OpenAI names Abilene as flagship Stargate site; Oracle began delivering GB200 racks in June 2025.
Campus expanded to 1.2 GW; 1.2 GW grid connection with batteries, solar, and gas turbine backup.

sites.name: Fairwater
sites.dek: Microsoft Fairwater sites in Mount Pleasant, Wisconsin and Atlanta, Georgia, linked by the AI WAN into one superfactory design.

location.text: Mount Pleasant, Wisconsin and Atlanta, Georgia

status.note: Wisconsin building 1 fully operational (23 Jun 2026); building 2 due 2028. Atlanta running since October 2025.

statusSegments.text: Wisconsin building 1 fully operational (23 Jun 2026); building 2 due 2028.

chips.countText: hundreds of thousands across the Fairwater design

usedFor.what: training frontier models and inference for leading AI workloads

cooling.text: Closed-loop liquid cooling; over 90% on water loop and about 10% outdoor air on hottest days; 172 fans, each 20 feet across

waterSegments.text: Initial fill equals what 20 homes use in a year (Atlanta); replaced only when water chemistry requires

water.text: Initial fill equals what 20 homes use in a year (Atlanta); replaced only when water chemistry requires; designed for 6+ years

network.text: 800 Gb/s GPU to GPU, two-tier Ethernet backend; AI WAN links sites across 120,000+ new fiber miles in the US

cost.text: About $4.7 billion local Wisconsin construction spend, 2024 to 2028

site.text: Wisconsin: 315 acres, three buildings, 1.2 million sq ft under roof

extraRows.label: Other figures
extraRows.text: Up to 72 Blackwell GPUs per rack; about 140 kW per rack and 1,360 kW per row

image.alt: Aerial view of Fairwater in Mount Pleasant, Wisconsin

notes.text: Microsoft claim: Fairwater will deliver 10 times the performance of the world's fastest supercomputer today.
Microsoft claim: Wisconsin is home to the world's most powerful supercomputer (23 Jun 2026 announcement).
Atlanta site uses grid power with 4x9 availability at 3x9 cost: no on-site generators or UPS for GPUs; on-site energy storage smooths swings.

updates.text: First Wisconsin facility fully operational; second facility scheduled for 2028.
Atlanta Fairwater site unveiled; began operation in October 2025.
Fairwater Wisconsin introduced: GB200 cluster, closed-loop cooling, two-story buildings.
